title: How Canada is Decoupling From the US
gist: Canada's share of trade with the US has fallen to a 30-plus-year low as Trump's tariffs, consumer boycotts and an Ottawa push for diversification drove non-US exports up more than 40% in twelve months, led by gold, metals and energy. Yet the US remains 8x larger than the next partner, decoupling is costly (business investment in factories and mines is falling), and the author argues Canada has gained leverage ahead of a likely USMCA renegotiation.
